questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Kite ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD. Its diagonals meet at E. Prove that AC ⊥ BD.
questions.prompt_markup: Kite ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD. Its diagonals meet at E. Prove that AC ⊥ BD.
questions.required_method: Prove △ABC ≅ △ADC (SSS) to get ∠BAE ≅ ∠DAE; then △ABE ≅ △ADE (SAS); then the angles at E form a congruent linear pair.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: SSS (AB = AD, CB = CD, AC shared); ∠BAC ≅ ∠DAC; SAS on △ABE and △ADE (AE shared); ∠AEB ≅ ∠AED, a linear pair, so 90°. Alternative: A and C are each equidistant from B and D, so AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD.
